Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name

  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key

  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable phone/tablet football career game with club transfers, match highlights, national competitions, and an off-pitch life.

## Requirements
- Include nation selection, weekly contract wages, club transfers, playable match highlights, gym training, dating, gambling with money, wearable mall clothes, hairstyles, TV, and games.
- Make the game suitable for phone/tablet.

## Decisions
- Implemented match gameplay as interactive 2D canvas rather than 3D.
- Gambling is optional and uses fictional in-game credits; harmful conduct and referee bribery were not implemented.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built a responsive single-page career game with player creation, nation selection, match controls and highlights, fictional World Cup and UEFA Champions League modes, life activities, penalty arcade, mall/wardrobe, hairstyles, transfers, player profile, and localStorage autosave.
- `node --check app.js` completed without errors.
- Installed Chromium and opened `http://localhost:3002` in Playwright.

### Active
- Browser QA is incomplete: only the initial page was opened; career creation, match play, and activities have not been tested.
- Browser reported one console error: 404 for `/favicon.ico`.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser QA at `http://localhost:3002`; capture and inspect a phone/tablet-friendly screenshot.
2. Test career creation, match play through full time, and key life/clubhouse activities; fix any issues found.
3. Optionally add a favicon to resolve the 404.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App entry point and responsive viewport metadata.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and mobile layout.
- `app.js`: Game state, UI rendering, match simulation, and career/life/clubhouse actions.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A local server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Match controls include touch buttons and WASD/arrow keys; Space shoots, E passes, Shift tackles.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable phone/tablet football career game with club transfers, match highlights, competitions, and off-pitch activities.

## Requirements
- Include nation selection, weekly contract wages, club transfers, playable match highlights, gym training, dating, fictional-credit gambling, wearable mall clothes, hairstyles, TV, and games.
- Make the game suitable for phone/tablet.

## Decisions
- Match gameplay uses an interactive 2D canvas rather than 3D.
- Gambling is optional and uses fictional in-game credits; harmful conduct and referee bribery were not implemented.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built a responsive single-page career game with player creation, nation selection, match controls/highlights, fictional World Cup and UEFA Champions League modes, life activities, penalty arcade, mall/wardrobe, hairstyles, transfers, player profile, and localStorage autosave.
- Verified `node --check app.js`.
- Browser-tested career creation, a full match and its rewards, training, Clubhouse transfer listings, mall, and style studio.
- Captured `screenshots/mobile-career.png` at 390×844; no horizontal-overflow check completed.

### Active
- Finish browser QA for remaining key interactions and inspect the mobile screenshot.
- Fix the remaining browser console error, a 404 for `/favicon.ico`.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `screenshots/mobile-career.png` and complete the mobile layout check.
2. Test dating, recovery, TV, arcade, fictional coin flip, transfer acceptance, and match controls/competitions.
3. Add a favicon or otherwise resolve the `/favicon.ico` 404; rerun browser console and syntax checks.

- `index.html`: App entry point and viewport metadata.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and mobile layout.
- `app.js`: Game state, UI rendering, match simulation, and career/life/clubhouse actions.
- `screenshots/mobile-career.png`: Captured mobile viewport for inspection.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; repository status showed project files as untracked.
- Local server is running at `http://localhost:3002`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable phone/tablet football career game with club transfers, match highlights, competitions, and off-pitch activities.

## Requirements
- Include nation selection, weekly contract wages, club transfers, playable match highlights, gym training, dating, fictional-credit gambling, wearable mall clothes, hairstyles, TV, and games.
- Make the game suitable for phone/tablet.

## Decisions
- Match gameplay uses an interactive 2D canvas rather than 3D.
- Gambling is optional and uses fictional in-game credits; harmful conduct and referee bribery were not implemented.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built a responsive single-page career game with player creation, nation selection, match controls/highlights, fictional World Cup and UEFA Champions League modes, life activities, penalty arcade, mall/wardrobe, hairstyles, transfers, player profile, and localStorage autosave.
- Verified `node --check app.js`; browser-tested career creation, a full match and rewards, training, Clubhouse listings, mall, style studio, recovery, and dating.
- Confirmed at 390px viewport width the document scroll width is 375px, with no horizontal overflow.
- Added `favicon.svg` and linked it from `index.html`.

### Active
- Finish browser QA for TV, arcade, fictional coin flip, transfer acceptance, and match controls/competitions.
- Reload and recheck browser console to confirm the favicon 404 is resolved.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reload the page and verify `/favicon.ico` no longer causes a console error.
2. Test TV, arcade, coin flip, transfer acceptance, and match controls/competition selection.
3. Verify the mobile screenshot shows the intended career screen; current `screenshots/mobile-career.png` was captured while on Clubhouse style studio.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App entry point and favicon link.
- `favicon.svg`: App icon added to resolve the favicon request.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and mobile layout.
- `app.js`: Game state, UI rendering, match simulation, and career/life/clubhouse actions.
- `screenshots/mobile-career.png`: Existing mobile viewport capture; currently shows the style studio, not the career screen.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Local server is running at `http://localhost:3002`.
- The first match completed successfully with a 1–0 win and £9,300 reward; training changed fitness and energy as expected.
- Last browser console check still showed `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found) @ http://localhost:3002/favicon.ico:0`; it was before reloading after the favicon change.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, phone/tablet-friendly football career game with club transfers, match highlights, competitions, and off-pitch activities.

## Requirements
- Include nation selection, weekly contract wages, club transfers, playable match highlights, gym training, dating, fictional-credit gambling, wearable mall clothes, hairstyles, TV, and games.
- Make the game suitable for phone/tablet.

## Decisions
- Match gameplay uses an interactive 2D canvas rather than 3D.
- Gambling is optional and uses fictional in-game credits; harmful conduct and referee bribery were not implemented.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built a responsive single-page career game with player creation, nation selection, match controls/highlights, fictional World Cup and UEFA Champions League modes, life activities, penalty arcade, mall/wardrobe, hairstyles, transfers, player profile, and localStorage autosave.
- Verified `node --check app.js`; browser-tested career creation, a full match and rewards, training, Clubhouse listings, mall, style studio, recovery, and dating.
- Verified 390px viewport has no horizontal overflow (document scroll width 375px).
- Added `favicon.svg` and linked it in `index.html`; reloaded and confirmed browser console has no errors.
- Browser-tested TV channel selection and energy reward, all three penalty arcade kicks and prize, and a fictional coin flip (stake lost; balance changed from £21,770 to £21,670).

### Active
- Finish browser QA for transfer acceptance, match controls, and competition selection.
- Update `screenshots/mobile-career.png` to show the career screen; current screenshot shows Clubhouse style studio.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test accepting a transfer offer and verify club and weekly wage update.
2. Test match controls and competition selection.
3. Capture a fresh mobile career screenshot and recheck the mobile viewport.
4. Check the browser console after the remaining QA.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App entry point and favicon link.
- `favicon.svg`: App icon.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and mobile layout.
- `app.js`: Game state, UI rendering, match simulation, and career/life/clubhouse actions.
- `screenshots/mobile-career.png`: Existing mobile screenshot; currently shows the wrong screen.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Local server is running at `http://localhost:3002`.
- The first match completed successfully with a 1–0 win and £9,300 reward; training changed fitness and energy as expected.
- TV, arcade, and coin flip are browser-tested; the arcade awarded £300 for scoring 2/3 penalties.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, phone/tablet-friendly football career game with club transfers, match highlights, competitions, and off-pitch activities.

## Requirements
- Include nation selection, weekly contract wages, club transfers, playable match highlights, gym training, dating, fictional-credit gambling, wearable mall clothes, hairstyles, TV, and games.
- Make the game suitable for phone/tablet.

## Decisions
- Match gameplay uses an interactive 2D canvas rather than 3D.
- Gambling is optional and uses fictional in-game credits; harmful conduct and referee bribery were not implemented.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the responsive career game, including player creation, nation selection, matches, fictional World Cup and UEFA Champions League modes, life activities, penalty arcade, mall/wardrobe, hairstyles, transfers, profile, and localStorage autosave.
- Verified `node --check app.js` and browser-tested career creation, a full match and rewards, training, Clubhouse, mall, style studio, recovery, dating, TV, penalty arcade, and fictional coin flip.
- Verified no horizontal overflow at 390px viewport; added `favicon.svg` and linked it in `index.html`.
- Confirmed browser console had no errors during earlier QA and recent TV/arcade/gambling checks.
- Tested penalty arcade sequence and prize; tested coin flip with a £100 stake, reducing balance from £21,770 to £21,670.

### Active
- Finish browser QA for transfer acceptance, match controls, and competition selection.
- Update `screenshots/mobile-career.png` to show the career screen; current screenshot shows Clubhouse style studio.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test accepting a transfer offer and verify club and weekly wage update.
2. Test match controls and competition selection.
3. Capture a fresh mobile career screenshot and recheck the mobile viewport.
4. Check the browser console after remaining QA.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App entry point and favicon link.
- `favicon.svg`: App icon.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and mobile layout.
- `app.js`: Game state, UI rendering, match simulation, and career/life/clubhouse actions.
- `screenshots/mobile-career.png`: Existing mobile screenshot to replace.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Local server is running at `http://localhost:3002`.
- The first match completed successfully with a 1–0 win and £9,300 reward; training changed fitness and energy as expected.
- Recent QA exercised TV channel selection and energy reward, all three penalty arcade kicks and prize, and coin flip.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, phone/tablet-friendly football career game with club transfers, match highlights, competitions, and off-pitch activities.

## Requirements
- Include nation selection, weekly contract wages, club transfers, playable match highlights, gym training, dating, fictional-credit gambling, wearable mall clothes, hairstyles, TV, and games.
- Make the game suitable for phone/tablet.

## Decisions
- Match gameplay uses an interactive 2D canvas rather than 3D.
- Gambling is optional and uses fictional in-game credits; harmful conduct and referee bribery were not implemented.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the responsive career game, including player creation, nation selection, matches, fictional World Cup and UEFA Champions League modes, life activities, penalty arcade, mall/wardrobe, hairstyles, transfers, profile, and localStorage autosave.
- Verified `node --check app.js` and browser-tested career creation, a full match and rewards, training, Clubhouse, mall, style studio, recovery, dating, TV, penalty arcade, and fictional coin flip.
- Tested accepting a transfer offer and signing a contract; match controls (pass and shoot) and competition selection (UEFA Champions League and World Cup).
- Updated `screenshots/mobile-career.png` to a 390×844 career-screen screenshot and checked mobile document width (375px at 390px viewport).

### Active
- Investigate and fix the browser console error in `endMatch()` occurring after navigating away from a match; rerun browser QA afterward.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `endMatch()` in `app.js`; guard or clear delayed match callbacks that access missing DOM elements after navigation.
2. Repeat match and navigation QA, then confirm the browser console has no errors.
3. Recheck transfer acceptance, match controls, competition selection, and the 390px screenshot if the fix changes the UI.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, rendering, match simulation, and career/life/clubhouse actions; contains the unresolved `endMatch()` error.
- `index.html`: App entry point and favicon link.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and mobile layout.
- `screenshots/mobile-career.png`: Current mobile career screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Local server is running at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Browser console reported `TypeError: Cannot set properties of null (setting 'textContent')` at `endMatch` (`app.js:22:1354`), called from a timer (`app.js:14:970`); it occurred after navigating away from a match.

content.text:
playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

## Compact MVP plan

Build one **“Off the Pitch”** menu that connects the four features without expanding the whole game at once:

1. **Girlfriend relationship**
   - Add a simple relationship meter and a few short choices: supportive message, date, or skip.
   - Make outcomes friendly and low-stakes—small morale or story changes, never a penalty that blocks career progress.

2. **Switch clubs**
   - Add a **Transfer Offers** screen with a small set of fictional clubs, each showing role, playing time, and salary.
   - Let players accept or decline; preserve their career stats and make the change clear before confirming.

3. **Mall visit**
   - Start with a compact, stylized mall scene and a few tappable destinations rather than a large open world.
   - Use large mobile-friendly hotspots for a café/date, clothing shop, and arcade. Keep visits short and optional.

4. **Cartoon scuffle**
   - Make this an occasional, clearly fictional slapstick minigame—not a realistic combat system.
   - Use simple **punch / kick** buttons and a few selectable, non-graphic targets such as a rival’s padded gear or a comically oversized prop. Pair actions with silly, non-abusive taunts.
   - Show exaggerated effects—boing sounds, stars, goofy reactions—with no blood, injury detail, or real-world fighting instructions. Let players back out, and resolve it with a harmless joke or brief morale change.

**Mobile priorities:** large buttons, short scenes, clear back/skip controls, and no precision-dependent gestures. Ship the relationship flow, transfer screen, and a small mall first; add the scuffle as an optional event after those core interactions feel consistent.
</subagent>

## Objective
- Continue building Touchline, a playable, phone/tablet-friendly football career game.
- Add a girlfriend, club switching, a freely explorable mall, and optional stylized arcade fights with punch/kick controls and selectable targets.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing career game and its features.
- Make the mall explorable and fights playable with punch, kick, and body-part target selection.
- Include insults/taunts during fights.

## Decisions
- Keep fighting fictional, stylized, non-graphic, and arcade-like rather than realistic.
- Earlier features use interactive 2D gameplay rather than 3D; no decision has been made to add 3D combat.

## Work State
### Completed
- Fixed match navigation cleanup and guarded the full-time competition label update in `app.js`.
- Browser-tested leaving a match, returning to Career, and changing the competition label; `node --check app.js` and browser console checks passed.

### Active
- Inspect and extend existing girlfriend/dating, club transfer, and mall systems.
- Design and implement an explorable mall and optional stylized fight sequence with punch/kick, target selection, and playful insults.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Inspect the remaining findings on existing dating, transfer, and mall hooks in `app.js` and `style.css`.
2. Implement the requested connected features, keeping interactions mobile-friendly and fights clearly fictional/non-graphic.
3. Run syntax checks and browser QA for girlfriend, club switching, mall exploration, and fight controls.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, screen routing, career/life/clubhouse activities, and existing girlfriend/transfer/mall logic.
- `style.css`: Responsive styling and mobile layout.
- `index.html`: App entry point.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e447fdba0ffe7TzAsHSflY8DCy" state="completed">
## Confirmed gameplay issues

- **“Drive into the box” can be completed without carrying the ball.** Player movement updates `maxX` before checking possession, and the challenge succeeds based only on `maxX`. Moving past the threshold off the ball therefore counts as carrying it into the attacking area.  
  **Refs:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:81`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L81), [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:94`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L94)  
  **Fix:** Require possession when the player reaches the box, or track whether the player advanced with the ball.

- **“Find the far corner” does not check for a far-corner shot.** The challenge succeeds on any goal. A shot is considered on target across a broad goal area, while the accuracy calculation actually favors aiming toward the center.  
  **Refs:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:52`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L52), [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:89`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L89), [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:94`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L94)  
  **Fix:** Define a far-corner target zone and make challenge success depend on aiming or scoring in that zone—or rename the challenge.

- **“Make your mark” counts off-target attempts as shots on goal.** The shot counter increments before the code checks whether the aim was on target, and the challenge succeeds on that counter alone.  
  **Refs:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:56`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L56), [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:89`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L89), [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:94`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L94)  
  **Fix:** Track on-target shots separately, or change the objective to “attempt a shot.”

- **Scenario matches also advance the persistent career.** At full time, the game records an appearance, processes wages and a result bonus, reduces fitness and contract time, and advances the week; this happens regardless of whether the scenario challenge was completed.  
  **Ref:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:95`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L95)  
  This behavior is confirmed; whether it is a bug depends on intent. If scenarios are meant as practice, separate them from career progression. Otherwise, make the career consequences clear in the scenario UI.

## Name entry and swipe UX

- **No confirmed name-entry bug found.** The entry is limited to 30 characters, trimmed, and rejected if blank; player names are escaped when displayed.  
  **Refs:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:6`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L6), [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:8`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L8), [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:11`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L11)

- **Swipe shooting has explicit instructions and checks for possession and a forward aim.** The gesture must start near the player to enter aim mode, and a sufficiently long swipe then triggers the shot. A possible UX improvement is to make the aim-start area and valid target area more apparent, so players can tell why a gesture did or did not register.  
  **Refs:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:73`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L73), [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:78`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L78), [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:80`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L80), [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:89`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L89)

## Scenario count

The **225 playable scenarios** are generated by combining 5 lanes, 5 match states, and 9 challenges. The count is consistent with the generator; I found no issue with the total itself.  
**Refs:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:37`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L37)–[`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:67`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js#L67)
</subagent>

## Objective
- Let players choose an in-game name and play 3D-style football highlights with swipe-to-shoot controls.
- Provide more than 200 playable scenarios integrated with match setup and gameplay.

## Requirements
- Allow the user to enter a name for their player.
- Highlights should be 3D; players swipe to shoot and start from a scenario.
- Include more than 200 scenarios.

## Decisions
- Use the existing player creation screen’s name field; save and display the entered name in career/profile screens.
- Generate scenarios from combinations of starting positions, match states, and objectives.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added player name entry, Enter-key submission, empty-name validation, and escaped display in career/profile screens.
- Added a perspective-projected pitch, drag/swipe controls, opponent movement, and shot sequences.
- Added 225 generated scenarios with selection/random loading, objective display, scenario starting states, and objective completion tracking.
- Improved objective progress feedback; scenario reload resets full-time controls/status.
- Fixed scenario objective checks: “Find the far corner” now requires a scored corner shot; “Make your mark” requires an on-target shot; “Drive into the box” tracks advancing with possession.
- Verified scenario objectives, scenario picker count, scenario loading, responsive layouts, swipe-shot behavior, and runtime without page errors.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Final verification of the latest objective-logic changes and review of remaining gameplay/UX issues.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run syntax and browser checks after the latest objective changes, especially far-corner scoring and possession-based box progress.
2. Review and report the completed implementation and any remaining UX caveats.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Player creation, match rendering, controls, scenario generation/objectives, and gameplay.
- `style.css`: Pitch, responsive layout, swipe HUD, scenario picker, and shot-sequence styles.
- `index.html`: App entry point loading `app.js`.

## Important Context
- `app.js` contains two `renderMatch` declarations; the later swipe-first implementation around line 73 takes precedence.
- Changes remain uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Scenario matches currently advance persistent career stats, wages, fitness, contract time, and week at full time; whether this is intended depends on whether scenarios are practice or career matches.
- Existing browser checks used `http://127.0.0.1:8765`; screenshots are `/tmp/opencode/match-desktop.png` and `/tmp/opencode/match-mobile.png`.

## Objective

## Requirements
- Allow users to enter a player name and display it in career/profile screens.
- Support swipe-to-shoot controls and scenario-based gameplay.
- Include more than 200 playable scenarios.

## Decisions
- Reuse the player creation screen’s name field and save the entered name.
- Generate scenarios from combinations of positions, match states, and objectives.

- (none)

- `style.css`: Pitch, responsive layout, swipe HUD, scenario picker, and shot sequences.

## Objective
- Build out the football career game with working match, driving, and training gameplay, plus a customizable house with purchasable, placeable items that persist.

## Requirements
- Let users name their player and display the name in career/profile screens.
- Support swipe-to-shoot controls, over 200 playable match scenarios, 3D-feeling highlights, a visible goal, and a responsive goalkeeper.
- Add driving to games and hands-on training with swipe and click controls.
- Let players buy house customizations, see owned items in their house, choose placements, and persist them.

## Decisions
- Reuse the player creation screen’s name field and save the entered name.
- Generate scenarios from combinations of positions, match states, and objectives.
- Training earns +1 OVR and +5 fitness for five or more hits, and costs 8 energy.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added player naming, validation, and escaped name display.
- Added projected-pitch match controls, generated 225 scenarios, objective tracking, and shot sequences.
- Added Drive and Training navigation, routes, activity cleanup, and playable activity loops with keyboard/touch controls.
- Driving reaches an arrival state and offers a Matchday continuation.
- Training updates rating, fitness, energy, and saves progress.
- Added responsive CSS for Drive and Training screens.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed after these changes.

### Active
- Add purchasable house decorations, a house view, placement controls, and save persistence.
- Verify shot animation CSS uses `--shot-dy` and `--keeper-y`.
- Browser-test the new Drive and Training activities and review the full UI.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement house shopping, owned-item display, placement controls, and persistence.
2. Check shot animation keyframes for `--shot-dy` and `--keeper-y`; add or correct them if needed.
3. Run browser checks for Drive, Training, and house flows, then re-run syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, routing, match logic, and newly added Drive/Training activities.
- `style.css`: App styling, shot animation styling, and responsive Drive/Training styles.
- `index.html`: App entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- `app.js` has duplicate declarations for several match functions; later declarations take precedence.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build out the football career game with playable match, driving, and training activities, plus a customizable house with purchasable decorations, placement, and save persistence.

## Requirements
- Let users name their player and display the name in career/profile screens.
- Support swipe-to-shoot controls, over 200 match scenarios, 3D-feeling highlights, a visible goal, and a responsive goalkeeper.
- Add playable driving and hands-on training with swipe and click controls.
- Let players buy house decorations, place owned items, and persist purchases and placements.

## Decisions
- Reuse the player creation name field and save the entered name.
- Generate scenarios from combinations of positions, match states, and objectives.
- Training earns +1 OVR and +5 fitness for five or more hits, and costs 8 energy.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added player naming, validation, and escaped name display.
- Added projected-pitch match controls, 225 generated scenarios, objective tracking, and shot sequences.
- Added Drive and Training navigation, routes, activity loops, and responsive styling.
- Driving reaches an arrival state and offers a Matchday continuation.
- Training updates rating, fitness, energy, and saves progress.
- Added house catalog purchases, an interactive room with placement/move/pickup controls, owned-item inventory, and saved `houseItems`/`housePlacements`.
- Added responsive styling for the house room, decorations, inventory, and shop.
- Verified `node --check app.js`; checked that shot animation keyframes exist.
- Reloaded the app in Chromium and confirmed house functions are defined without browser exceptions.

### Active
- Browser-test the house purchase/place/pickup/persistence flow and Drive/Training activities.
- Run final syntax and diff checks after the latest styling changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`.
2. Browser-test house purchase, placement, pickup, and persistence; also test Drive and Training.
3. Review the final changes and report results.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, routes, match logic, Drive/Training activities, and house implementation.
- `style.css`: App and activity styling, shot animations, and house styling.
- `index.html`: App entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- `app.js` has duplicate declarations for several match functions; later declarations take precedence.

## Objective
- Build a playable football career game with match, driving, training, and a customizable, persistent house.
- Make the driving activity first-person with improved graphics.

## Requirements
- Let users name their player and display the name in career/profile screens.
- Support swipe-to-shoot controls, over 200 match scenarios, 3D-feeling highlights, a visible goal, and a responsive goalkeeper.
- Add playable driving and hands-on training with swipe and click controls.
- Let players buy house decorations, place owned items, and persist purchases and placements.
- Driving should be first-person and have good graphics.

## Decisions
- Reuse the player creation name field and save the entered name.
- Generate scenarios from combinations of positions, match states, and objectives.
- Training earns +1 OVR and +5 fitness for five or more hits, and costs 8 energy.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added player naming, match scenarios and controls, Drive and Training activities, and house shopping, placement, and persistence.
- Browser-tested house purchase, placement, persistence, and pickup; tested driving controls and training rewards.
- Replaced the driving canvas renderer with a first-person perspective scene, including road depth, roadside scenery, traffic, dashboard, instrument cluster, and steering wheel.

### Active
- Validate the new first-person driving view in the browser and refine if needed.
- Run final syntax and diff checks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`.
2. Reload the game in Chromium and inspect the first-person driving view at desktop and mobile sizes.
3. Review the final changes and report results.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, driving renderer, match, training, and house features.
- `style.css`: App and activity styling, including responsive layouts.
- `index.html`: App entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Earlier browser tests passed for house persistence, driving steering, and training rewards; the updated driving graphics have not yet been browser-tested.

## Objective
- Build a playable football career game with match, driving, training, and a customizable, persistent house.
- Make the driving activity first-person with improved graphics.

## Requirements
- Let users name their player and display the name in career/profile screens.
- Support swipe-to-shoot controls, over 200 match scenarios, 3D-feeling highlights, a visible goal, and a responsive goalkeeper.
- Add playable driving and hands-on training with swipe and click controls.
- Let players buy house decorations, place owned items, and persist purchases and placements.
- Driving should be first-person and have good graphics.

## Decisions
- Reuse the player creation name field and save the entered name.
- Generate scenarios from combinations of positions, match states, and objectives.
- Training earns +1 OVR and +5 fitness for five or more hits, and costs 8 energy.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added player naming, match scenarios and controls, Drive and Training activities, and house shopping, placement, and persistence.
- Browser-tested house purchase, placement, persistence, and pickup; tested driving controls and training rewards.
- Replaced the driving canvas renderer with a first-person perspective scene featuring a detailed road, scenery, traffic, dashboard, instrument cluster, and steering wheel.
- Tested the driving view in Chromium at desktop and mobile sizes; both rendered without JavaScript errors.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Review final changes and report results.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, first-person driving renderer, match, training, and house features.
- `style.css`: App and activity styling, including responsive layouts.
- `index.html`: App entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- The server already listening at `http://127.0.0.1:3000/` served the updated game; an extra `./start.sh` attempt failed because port 3000 was in use.
